note: Real AdvoKC evidence updates (published on promisetracker.ng), used as STYLE examples for the writer eval. Captured 2026-11-18.

examples.text: NPA Unclogs Apapa Port to Ease Container Movement The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has dismantled over 1,500 illegally parked trucks and unauthorised checkpoints at the Apapa port corridors as part of measures to eliminate traffic congestion, restore order, improve cargo movement and reduce extortion. The Authority also disclosed that it has expanded barge operations to move over 30 per cent of containerised cargo through inland waterways. These efforts are clearly aimed at decongesting the Apapa port by the government to improve commerce. This promise is rated In the works

ASUU-FG SIGNS AGREEMENT AS ASUU AGREES 40% SALARY INCREMENT The Federal Government (FG) and Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has reached an agreement on increase in renumeration, creation of the National Research Council and other important issues. The agreement marks a milestone in resolving age long dispute between the FG and ASUU concerning the welfare of universities academic staff. This promise is rated in the works

FOOD INFLATION COOLS TO 16.87% IN SEPTEMBER In recent months food inflation in the country has seen steady decline. Recent data show food inflation has begun to ease somewhat. For example, food inflation dropped to 16.87 % in September 2025 from 21.87 % in August. This reduction in food prices showcases government actions in combating higher food prices is gradually yielding results. This promise is rated in the works.

UNLOCKING THE BLUE ECONOMY: THE NIGERIAN PORT OVERHAUL A sweeping modernization initiative has begun, covering Apapa, Tin Can Island, Warri, Calabar, Port Harcourt, including civil works, dredging, berth upgrades. It has led to increased trade volumes. A $1billion overhaul of the ports across the country has deliver record trade volumes and revive confidence in the nation’s blue-economy. Other ports upgrades like terminal upgrades in Onne port and the continued dredging of the Lekki sea port are efforts the government is taking to modernise and improve the country's ports. This promise is rated in the works.

RAIL TO MARADI: A PROMISE IN PROGRESS This project was originally approved under President Buhari’s administration; contract awarded to Portuguese company Mota-Engil under an MoU for design, construction and rolling-stock supply. Project approved (~US$1.96-$2 billion) in 2020. Originally, government said the line would be completed by 2026. More recent update says full completion postponed to March 2027, while segment to Katsina is expected by December 2025, overall the completion satge of the project is at 60%. This promise is rated in the works.

Fedral Government dredges Inland waterways to improve transportation The Federal Government through the minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola has made it known that they have dredged p to 2,000 kilometers of inland waterways to ensure year-round access to inland waterways. the dredging of the inland ways for increased water transportation shows the Government commitment to ensuring smooth inland water trasportation. This promise is rated in the works.

AVIATION: FG TO REBUILD TERMINAL ONE OF MURITALA MUHAMMED AIRPORT Nigeria Federal Government has concluded plans to rebuild terminal one of Murital Muhammed airport in lagos for 712.26 billion million naira . this move is said to improve the service delivery of the busiest airport in the country. The 1979-built Terminal One, which houses Wings D and E, will be stripped to its structural frame and reconfigured into a modern terminal that meets global standards. Years of neglect and surging passenger numbers have left the building obsolete, forcing temporary repairs over time. This promise is rated in the works

LAGOS - KANO RAIL: FG Secures Full Funding for Kano-Kaduna Standard Rail Project The FG has secured funding for the completion of the Kano-Kaduna standard rail project part of the stretch of the Lagos-Kano rail project, the China Development Bank (CDB) had in January 2025 granted a loan of €245 million ($254.76 million). The government sees the year 2026 as the completion year for the project as the full funding for the project has been secured. This promise is rated in the works

President Tinubu newest loan request to the legislative to cater for important infrastructural projects ongoing around the country, one of the promise in the list us the Port-Harcourt - Maiduguri rail project. The president requested to borrow $3 billion for the completion of the project. This promise is rated in the works.

Federal Government Launches Ultramodern Textile Hub in Maiduguri to Boost Industrial Growth The federal government has pledged to establish industrial hubs in northern Nigeria, particularly textile manufacturing centers, to spur economic growth in the region and the country at large. In line with this commitment, the government inaugurated one of Nigeria’s largest ultramodern fashion manufacturing hubs in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital. The facility is projected to create over 48,000 jobs, marking a significant step toward industrial development in the region. this promise is rated in the works.

Senate Pressures Aviation Regulators Over Rising Airfares and Consumer Protection The Senate’s main actions have been oversight and pressure on regulators rather than legislation. In December 2025, the Senate summoned the Minister of Aviation and major aviation stakeholders over sharp increases in airfares and concerns about consumer exploitation. Senators argued that passengers were being priced out of air travel and demanded stronger protections . This promise is rated in the works

10th Senate Focuses on Oversight of Defence Procurement, Not Creation of Central System Within the 10th Senate, there is no identifiable Senate-originated bill establishing a central defence procurement authority or a unified defence procurement system for the armed forces and security agencies. The Senate has instead focused on oversight of defence spending and procurement practices through the Senate Committee on Defence . In February 2026, the committee criticised delays and fragmentation in defence budget implementation and called for more transparent and timely use of military funds. This promise is rated Stalled.

10th Senate Expands Public Access to Legislative Records, Though Archive Remains Incomplete The 10th Senate has created and expanded a central online archive through the National Assembly website, where citizens can now access: Senate bills and bill-tracking pages Daily order papers Votes and proceedings Hansard records of Senate debates Committee information Legislative publications and reports Live and archived plenary videos The National Assembly website now includes dedicated sections for: Bills Tracker Order Papers Votes & Proceedings Hansard Publications / Legislative Digest Search Documents and Open Data Portal Although, most of the records are not up to date and needs to be properly updated. This promise is rated compromised.

The 10th Senate has begun considering constitutional amendment proposals to move several subjects—including aviation, drugs and poisons, marriage, labour, and aspects of trade and commerce from the Exclusive Legislative List to the Concurrent List. The aim is to give states greater authority to legislate and act in these areas rather than leaving them solely under federal control. Within the Senate, the only recent devolution-related constitutional bill publicly recorded is a general “ Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Alteration) Bill, 2025” sponsored by Senator Sunday Karimi SB.855, which passed first reading in June 2025. This promise is rated stalled.

UBEC Amendments Bill Stuck at First reading. Two amendment bills SB. 31 and SB 259 are two amendments bills concerning the amendment of the existing Universal Basic Education Act. However, based on the latest Senate bills record, it appears the bill has not progressed beyond introduction/first reading. This promise is rated in the works

Senate Advances Nigerian Ports Authority Amendment Bill as Port Reform Efforts Continue The 10th Senate has begun legislative work connected to amending the Nigerian Ports Authority Act. A bill titled the “Nigerian Ports Authority Act (Amendment) Bill, 2024". The bill SB02 sponsored by Senator Umar Sodiq Suleiman has since scaled second reading and awaiting committee report. This promise is rated in the works

Senate Passed Audit Bill, Waiting for Presidential Assent. The 10th senate on 17th of December, 2025 passed the amendment of the Audit Ordinance of 1956, a colonial-era law enacted 69 years ago, paving way for a new modern public audit framework in the country. The law still require the president assent before it can be implemented. This promise is rated kept

HB 790: National Inland Waterways Authority Act (Repeal and Enactment) Bill, 2023 Passed first rading, Awaiting second reading. HB 790 a bill for the National Inland Waterways Authority Act (Repeal and Enactment) has passed second reading and awaiting committee report in the house of representatives has passed first reading at the senate , the bill was sponsored by the Senate leader Sen. Bamidele, Michael Opeyemi . This promise is rated in the works

SENATE PASS INVESTMENTS AND SECURITIES (Repeal and Enactment) Bill 2024 FOR THIRD READING On December 4, 2024. The senate passed the Investments and Securities (Repeal and Enactment) Bill 2024 for its third reading. The bill sponsored by the Senate leader Opeyemi Bamidele, the bill aimed to safeguarding the integrity of the securities market, preventing market abuse, insider trading, and other fraudulent trade practices while ensuring fair and lawful operations. This promise is rated Kept

SENATE MOVES TO AMEND TERRORISM LAW; SEEK DEATH PENALTY FOR KIDNAPPER S The senate on 27th November commence amendment of existing terrorism law, after a heated debate on anti-terrorism fight a day before. The notable discussion is the classification of kidnapping as terrorism and death penalty being applicable. The motion for amendment was raised by the senate leader Opeyemi Bamidele, the bill follows resolutions reached just 24 hours earlier. This promise is rated in the works

Governor Yusuf upgrades slaughterhouses with N1.6 billion The Kano State Government, in collaboration with the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and the Lives and Livelihood Funds (LLF), inaugurated 20 modern public abattoirs strategically located in various local government areas, including Tudun Wada, Kura, Rano, Bebeji, Karaye, Kiru, and Gwarzo. Each facility is equipped with solar-powered boreholes, industrial freezers for meat storage, and animal dung disposal systems. This promise is rated, ‘ KEPT. ’

GOV. ENO HANDS OVER MANAGEMENT OF IBOM MODEL FARM TO STATE UNIVERSITY Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has handed over the management of Ibom Model Farm to Akwa Ibom State University (AKSU). He described the farm as more than an agricultural production centre, noting that it has been designed to offer recreational and tourism opportunities alongside food production. This promise is rated, ‘ IN THE WORKS. ’

Governor Eno Launches Tree Crop Revolution In Akwa Ibom Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has launched a tree crop revolution initiative with the procurement of 620,000 oil palm seedlings for distribution to farmers across the state. Governor Eno said the initiative forms part of his administration’s commitment to boosting agriculture, promoting food security, and expanding economic opportunities for farmers in the State. This promise is rated, ‘IN THE WORKS.’

40 out of the promised 50 CNG buses arrives in Uyo The state government ordered a total of 50 factory-built CNG buses to ease the high cost of transportation. As of August 2026, 40 of these buses have arrived in Uyo in batches from Turkey. The mass transit rollout features electronic ticketing and tracking devices to connect all 31 local government areas affordably This promise is rated, ‘IN THE WORKS.’

Gov. Abba Yusuf partners with key private sectors for the one-stop-shop for all agric value chain. Governor Yusuf’s promise to establish a priva ﻿ te sector-driven agro-industrial estate has integrated directly into the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) framework, backed by a ₦130 million direct program allocation alongside joint funding from the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and key partnership with Afcott Grains Ltd and t he Nigerian Commodity Exchange (NCX). This framework directly links local farmers to formal national and international commodity markets. Therefore, This promise is rated, ‘ IN THE WORKS ’.

Oyo government births new solid waste management system The Oyo State Government has flagged off the first phase of waste segregation across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), with the distribution of designated bins at the State Secretariat, Ibadan. This is coming after three years in office. Therefore, this promise is rated, ‘ COMPROMISED.’

Oyo Gender Inclusion Promise 'Compromised' After Sacking of Women Affairs Commissioner. Gov. Seyi Makinde of Oyo State has sacked the state Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Inclusion, Mrs Toyin Balogun. The Commissioner for Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperative, Alhaja Fausat Sanni, has been redeployed to replace Balogun at the Ministry of Women Affairs, with immediate effect. Dropping the number of women commissioners from 4 to 3: Health (Dr. Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi), Women Affairs (Alhaja Faosat Joke Sanni), and Youth & Sports (Dr. Wasilat Adegoke). Therefore, this promise is rated ‘ COMPROMISED’.

Governor Aiyedatiwa Light up Akure Market. An independent nighttime verification at Akure Market confirmed that newly installed solar streetlights are fully operational. This infrastructural update provides adequate illumination across the trading areas, directly fulfilling the governor's pledge to support women traders by enabling evening business hours. This promise is rated, ‘ KEPT ’

Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa implements new baseline wage. Ondo State has implemented a ₦73,000 minimum wage for civil servants, with labor unions immediately calling for further increases to align with current economic realities. The development highlights the ongoing tension between state wage promises and demands for higher compensation amidst rising living costs. This promise is rated, ‘KEPT.’

The Akwa Ibom govt. is set to launch Arise Park by September 2026. The state government has invested roughly N30.2 billion into the project. After delaying a soft opening originally planned for December 2025 to ensure flawless finishing, the government has set an official launch for September 2026 . This promise is rated, ‘ IN THE WORKS. ’

Rehabilitation of Oluku Market and Restoration of Electricity Underway On Sunday, October 18, 2026, rehabilitation activities at the burnt Oluku Market were observed to have commenced, with workers removing debris . Officials of the state electricity company were also seen erecting new electricity poles as part of efforts to restore electricity to the area. This promise is rated, ‘ IN THE WORKS.’

GOVERNOR MONDAY OKPEBHOLO PROMISED TO BEGIN RECONSTRUCTION OF THE UWASOTA-UWELU ROAD On Friday, September 25, the Governor of Edo State, Sen. Monday Okpebholo promised to begin reconstruction of the Uwasota-Uwelu Road ; he said this when he paid a visit to the Traders of Uwelu Spare Parts Market. This promise is rated, ‘NOT YET RATED.’

Edo State Government Reshuffles Executive Cabinet, Swears in Hon Osifo and Others. On August 12, the Edo State Government reshuffled the State Executive Council and swore in Mr. Iriabekhai Kayode Jeffery as Commissioner for Mining and Mr. Martin Anayochukwu Oli as Commissioner for Inter-Ethnic Relations. On August 19, Hon. Washington Osifo was sworn in as Commissioner for Education. Following these appointments, the State Executive Council comprises 28 commissioners, including 3 female commissioners . This promise is rated ‘ BROKEN.’

Governor Monday Okpbholo Nominates Martin Oli As Commissioner-Designate On Friday, June 26, Governor Monday Okpebholo nominated Martin Oli as Commissioner-Designate, as announced in a statement issued by the Secretary to the Edo State Government. According to the statement, Mr. Oli's nomination will be forwarded to the Edo State House of Assembly for screening and confirmation. This promise is rated "BROKEN."

Ramat Park Flyover To Be Commissioned In November 2026 During a recent inspection tour of the ongoing construction of the Ramat Park Flyover, the Governor of Edo State announced that the President of Nigeria, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, will commission the project in November 2026. This promise is rated "IN THE WORKS."

Asphalt Laying Around the Ramat Park Flyover Corridor Recently, asphalt laying was seen to have commenced around the Ramat Park Flyover corridors and extended towards a section of the Aduwawa axis. According to the site engineer, the asphalt would be done on two layers with the first already commenced at the Ramat Park Flyover corridor. This promise is rated, "In the Works"

Oba Market Building yet to be Completed; Some Parts Remain Untouched On Friday, May 15, 2026, AdvoKC observed that although the Oba Market building gutted by fire some years ago is yet to be fully completed, significant progress has been made. Workers were seen actively engaged on-site; however, it was also noted that a section of the market is yet to be addressed by the construction team. This promise is rated, " IN THE WORKS."

Ramat Park Flyover closer to Completion During a recent visit to the Ramat Park flyover, AdvoKC observed that the project is nearing completion, with workers and heavy construction equipment still active on and beneath the flyover structure. A conversation with one of the consultant structural engineers indicated that while the flyover itself has been completed, minor ancillary works such as park landscaping and water channeling are still in progress. This promise is rated "IN THE WORKS."

Aduwawa Cattle and Kara Market remain in poor condition A recent visit by AdvoKC to the Aduwawa Cattle and Kara Market revealed that the market remains in poor condition, with the roads in a deplorable state and traders operating under unhygienic conditions. This promise is rated, " NOT YET RATED."

Gov. Monday Okepbeholo inspects the Udomi-Uwessa Teaching Hospital During a recent project inspection tour in Edo Central, the Governor of Edo State, Governor Monday Okpebholo, alongside Idris Abdulkareem , visited several ongoing projects, including the Udomi-Uwessa Teaching Hospital. At the project site, where construction is actively underway, noticeable progress was observed compared to the previous stage of development. This promise is rated "In the Works."

Bill to Alter INEC Appointments in Committee Stage HB 1589 is proposing that when appointing the Chairman of the Commission, the position should be advertised inviting suitable persons to apply, and qualified candidates shall be publicly interviewed by the National Judicial Council and be appointed by a simple majority votes of the members of the National Judicial Council. This promise is rated In the Works
